newsitem.title: INDIA: Cargo ship laden with steel sinks in India.
newsitem.headline: Cargo ship laden with steel sinks in India.

text.p: Panama-flag cargo ship M.V. Green Opal, carrying 70,000 tonnes of steel, sank in a river on Thursday near the eastern city of Calcutta, police and local news agencies said.
Senior police official K.K. Kalia told Reuters in Calcutta that the ship, on its way to Hong Kong, sank in the Hooghly river about 40 km (25 miles) from Calcutta.
"We know some crew members were rescued but details are awaited," Kalia said. Local news agencies said all 20 crew were rescued.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) said the ship sank after hitting a barge. It quoted Calcutta Port Trust officials as saying the captain, the chief officer and the second officer were Korean and the remaining crew were Filipino.
Port officials were drawing up plans to lift the damaged ship from the water, the news agency said.
It quoted officials as saying cargo traffic would be affected if the damaged ship was not removed within two days.
